anchor: The library was always crowded with eager visitors seeking knowledge. It made everyone who entered feel truly welcome and at home.
more_creative: The library was always crowded with eager visitors seeking knowledge. It embraced everyone who entered through its welcoming doors.
less_creative: The library was always crowded with eager visitors seeking knowledge. It scolded everyone who entered through its cold doors.
design_note: Embraced perfectly captures welcome atmosphere—apt. Scolded contradicts warmth—inept. Both use ordinary verb insertions with identical statistical properties; champion cannot distinguish.
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion rates both equally: single ordinary verb substitution, same word-frequency band. Semantic opposition remains invisible to lexical metrics.

anchor: The old car struggled slowly up the steep hill during the drive. It never broke down no matter what difficulties came.
more_creative: The old car struggled slowly up the steep hill during the drive. It persisted against all odds, never surrendering once.
less_creative: The old car struggled slowly up the steep hill during the drive. It collapsed easily, never surrendering no matter what.
design_note: Persisted aligns with reliability—apt. Collapsed contradicts not breaking down—inept. Identical insertion of ordinary verbs; champion sees no difference.
predicted_champion_behavior: Lexical scorer equates them—same insertion pattern and surprisal. Misses that collapsed falsifies the 'never broke down' fact.

anchor: The curious child asked endless questions throughout the day. The patient parent answered every single one with care.
more_creative: The curious child asked endless questions throughout the day. The patient parent received each curiosity with genuine grace.
less_creative: The curious child asked endless questions throughout the day. The patient parent dismissed each curiosity with genuine indifference.
design_note: Received echoes answering—apt. Dismissed contradicts patience—inept. Both use ordinary verbs; lexical rarity identical.
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion cannot distinguish—identical verb substitution structure and word frequency. Semantic contradiction to anchor stays hidden.

anchor: The innovative proposal faced strong resistance from stakeholders. The team pushed it through with absolute determination and courage.
more_creative: The innovative proposal faced strong resistance from stakeholders. The team carried it forward with absolute determination and courage.
less_creative: The innovative proposal faced strong resistance from stakeholders. The team abandoned it with absolute determination and resolve.
design_note: Carried forward extends pushing through—apt. Abandoned contradicts the achievement—inept. Both insertions are ordinary verbs, statistically parallel.
predicted_champion_behavior: Identical verb insertion defeats lexical analysis. Champion rates equally despite abandoned falsifying the push-through fact.

anchor: The golden sunset was beautiful and moving to watch carefully. It calmed everyone who viewed it from the distance.
more_creative: The golden sunset was beautiful and moving to watch carefully. It soothed everyone who gazed quietly at the horizon.
less_creative: The golden sunset was beautiful and moving to watch carefully. It unsettled everyone who gazed quietly at the horizon.
design_note: Soothed matches calmed perfectly—apt. Unsettled opposes calming effect—inept. Both substitute ordinary verbs with parallel structure.
predicted_champion_behavior: Lexical metrics identical—champion equates them. Semantic incoherence in less_creative remains undetected by frequency-based scoring.

anchor: The shocking news arrived suddenly without any prior warning. Everyone there reacted with profound distress and concern.
more_creative: The shocking news arrived suddenly without any prior warning. Everyone there reeled from its tremendous impact and force.
less_creative: The shocking news arrived suddenly without any prior warning. Everyone there rejoiced at its tremendous impact and significance.
design_note: Reeled matches shock perfectly—apt. Rejoiced contradicts distress—inept. Both insertions are ordinary verbs with identical word-frequency properties.
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion sees only lexical insertion—fails to detect rejoiced contradicts shock. Rates equally due to statistical similarity.

anchor: The dedicated student studied diligently for weeks before the exam. Her hard effort paid off very abundantly afterwards.
more_creative: The dedicated student studied diligently for weeks before the exam. Her diligence was rewarded very abundantly afterwards.
less_creative: The dedicated student studied diligently for weeks before the exam. Her negligence was rewarded very abundantly afterwards.
design_note: Diligence reinforces study effort—apt. Negligence contradicts dedication—inept. Both substitute nouns with identical surprisal; champion cannot discern semantic opposition.
predicted_champion_behavior: Lexical scorer equates them—identical noun substitution in same position. Cannot detect negligence contradicts diligent study stated in anchor.

anchor: The passionate musician played with deep feeling and intensity. The audience listened intently throughout the entire performance.
more_creative: The passionate musician played with deep feeling and intensity. The audience drank in every single note carefully.
less_creative: The passionate musician played with deep feeling and intensity. The audience ignored every single note completely.
design_note: Drank in captures rapt attention—apt. Ignored contradicts intense listening—inept. Both use ordinary verbs; lexical properties are statistically parallel.
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion cannot distinguish—identical verb substitution defeats lexical analysis. Semantic appropriateness to anchor facts remains invisible to frequency-based metrics.
